newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weaker, Tapis bucks trend to firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weaker, Tapis bucks trend to firm.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Friday with the Tapis premium bucking the market trend and firming in the face of a generally weaker market.
Market sources said a refinery paid a market premium of $1.20 per barrel for 600,000 barrels of Tapis from a producer. The cargo loads late March and early April.

At the same time 500,000 barrels of April loading Tapis were sold by the producer at OSP plus a single-digit premium. Traders said the sale could relate to offering the Tapis into the Bangchak tender for April crudes. The tender closes February 25 and is valid for one day.
The loss of production from the 90,000 bpd Griffin and 80,000 bpd Cossack fields because of an approaching storm was supporting the light sweet market.
Cossack had already halved its production because of a problem with gas dehydration when both fields went down on Thursday.
March availabilities of light sweet grades were hard to find with most Australian grades already placed and the Tapis producer saying it had sold out of March barrels.
Griffin is due for one-month's maintenance work during April and Cossack is due down for a week in March.
The producer said it might offer a cargo of Labuan at levels 15 cents over Tapis for March loading.
Day-earlier talk of a major selling a package of MidEast grades was confirmed, with a U.S. major buying Murban and Umm Shaif at even to ADNOC and Qatar Land at four cents under QGPC.

An Oman deal was heard at MPM +1 cents, but could not be confirmed, while a major was said to have sold an Umm Shaif cargo at ADNOC plus one cent. The Oman deal would indicate recent premiums of 3/4 cents were now falling.
